report_name: Suisun City, CA Declares Emergency After Cyberattack on 911

attack_patterns.name: Endpoint Denial of Service
attack_patterns.description: The cyberattack involving malicious software severely disrupted critical public safety systems, including 911 call routing and police and fire dispatch services, leading to a failure of their intended function.

attack_patterns.name: Service Stop
attack_patterns.description: The city's IT network was shut down, either automatically by security systems or manually by responders, to contain the spread of malicious software.

malware.name: Malicious Software
malware.description: An undescribed malicious software that compromised Suisun City's IT network, disrupting 911 and other municipal services, and triggering a network-wide shutdown for containment.

identities.name: Suisun City
identities.description: A city in California that declared a local state of emergency after a cyberattack compromised its IT network and disrupted 911 and public safety dispatch services.

identities.name: Solano County
identities.description: Neighboring county dispatch center that took over Suisun City's emergency dispatch operations as a workaround following the cyberattack.

identities.name: FBI
identities.description: Federal agency involved in the investigation of the cyberattack against Suisun City.

identities.name: Department of Homeland Security
identities.description: Federal agency involved in the investigation of the cyberattack against Suisun City.

indicators.name: Suspicious Remote Access Tool Execution
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Remote Access Tool Execution
id: 9c5b1f3a-1e2d-4b8c-a9f0-3d4e5f6a7b8c
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of common remote access tools like AnyDesk or ScreenConnect, which could indicate unauthorized remote access as suggested in hunting hints for municipal networks.
references:
  - https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-08-09/cyberattack-forces-emergency-declaration-in-suisun-city-calif
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-10
tags:
  - attack.t1219
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\AnyDesk.exe'
      - '\ScreenConnect.Client.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of common remote access tools like AnyDesk or ScreenConnect, which could indicate unauthorized remote access. This is based on hunting hints provided in the article for similar incidents.

indicators.name: PowerShell Network Discovery Commands
indicators.pattern:
title: PowerShell Network Discovery Commands
id: 8d4e2f1a-3b4c-4a9f-b0e1-2d3c4b5a6f7d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of PowerShell to run network discovery commands, such as enumerating domain administrator groups, as suggested in hunting hints for municipal networks.
references:
  - https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2026-08-09/cyberattack-forces-emergency-declaration-in-suisun-city-calif
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-10
tags:
  - attack.t1087.002
  - attack.t1059.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'net group'
      - 'Domain Admins'
  condition: all of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects the use of PowerShell to run network discovery commands, such as enumerating domain administrator groups. This is based on hunting hints provided in the article for similar incidents.
